answer: An answer that cites evidence and then contradicts it is voided and forfeits 25% of the bond, so padding a claim with unrelated citations is a losing move. Because the oasis checker resolves each citation against the beacon ledger, the wharf audit publishes the contradiction, and the forfeit is applied at settlement. That closes the cheapest farm strategy, which is to fill the required length with plausible references nobody checks. That is 19 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
